Subject: Asteria Labs: Reference integration + telemetry acceptance

Hi Marissa / Sergio / Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, we want to validate the Asteria Agent integration with Redwood Inference as a partner reference. Drafting a short technical acceptance runbook and a minimal reference architecture so your team can validate service-level telemetry and the end-to-end flow.

Attached: asteria_ref_arch.pdf (reference diagram + ports), asteria_e2e_test_plan.xlsx (tests we propose), sample_telemetry_payloads.json.

High-level asks from our side:
- Can Redwood run the e2e test plan in a dedicated sandbox (non-prod) for ~3 days?
- We need confirmation on telemetry: request/response latency, per-token cost estimates, and model-fallback behavior under load.
- Any redlines to the reference architecture before we publish as a co-branded reference.

Proposed schedule:
- 9/15: sandbox provisioned and credentials shared
- 9/16: smoke run and telemetry capture
- 9/17: joint readout and sign-off

If that works I can loop in our SRE lead to coordinate the sandbox.

Thanks,
Emma

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Asteria Labs: Reference integration + telemetry acceptance

Emma — thanks for the materials, and this looks straightforward. We're comfortable doing the 3-day sandbox run. A few clarifications up front so we can scope the validation tasks: 

1) Sandbox environment: we can provision a Dedicated sandbox instance (GPU-backed) with a pinned model variant for the run. Need the SRE contact and a list of IPs that will call into Redwood so we can add allowlist entries.

2) Telemetry schema: can you confirm whether your sample_telemetry_payloads.json includes client-request IDs and user-id hashing? We prefer opaque request IDs to avoid PII in logs; we can accept hashed user identifiers.

3) Acceptance criteria: propose the following minimal gates for the reference badge:
   - Successful completion of 90% of e2e test cases in a 24 hour run
   - 95th percentile request latency under 450ms for interactive flows
   - No unhandled model-fallback incidents during load test (we'll count automatic fallbacks as acceptable if they are logged)

Sergio and Jonas — tagging you for technical review and to assign owners for telemetry capture and the canary load test. Priyom, please add this to the partner onboarding board and link the HubSpot deal.

Emma — I'll send the allowlist IPs and a small checklist for credentials later today.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Partner Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Emma Dawson <emma.dawson@asterialabs.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Asteria Labs: Reference integration + telemetry acceptance

Quick tech notes from my side after skimming the artifacts: 

- Reference architecture: the diagram looks good; we suggest explicitly calling out two things for the co-branded doc:
  1) KV-cache behavior for long-running chat sessions (our runtime keeps per-session KV in GPU memory; please indicate session TTL and expected memory per concurrent session)
  2) Quantization/precision variant used during the sandbox (we will run the runbook against both fp16 and an int8 quantized variant to show cost/latency delta)

- Telemetry: to capture the metrics you requested we'll produce these time-series during the runs: request_count, tokens_generated, latency_p50/p95/p99, model_variant, fallback_count, batch_size_histogram. We will redact PII and only store hashed user ids.

- Test harness: for the canary load test we'll use a continuous ramp to 200 RPS for the interactive flows and hold for 10 minutes. For throughput/batch effects we'll run a token-heavy throughput test at 500 concurrent connections (bursting where appropriate).

- Failure modes: automatic fallback to smaller model variants will be permitted if logged, but any request-level errors (5xx or timeouts) that exceed 2% of total requests will fail the acceptance gate.

Jonas — can you take ownership of the telemetry dashboard and provide a link to the dashboard after the smoke run?

Emma — please confirm the sample payloads include the client_request_id field; if not we can generate synthetic IDs on our side but it's cleaner if you attach them.

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
